limits: Calls into other Modules are not followed: an operation that shows 0 queries may delegate them (OAuth, connections, event streams). Read the handler or probe it.
Interface calls, callbacks and closures passed to helpers are not followed; the estimate can undercount.
The estimate counts every branch and treats any loop over a non-literal bound as N, so a loop that rarely queries (cache miss, small fixed list) can be a false N+1. A probe settles it.
N is unknown; the probe measures shape (queries per row), not time.

findings.rationale: A :many query with no LIMIT returns every matching row, so response size and memory grow with the table.
findings.fix: add LIMIT $n, ideally with keyset pagination

findings.message: sorts items by created_at with no index to read it in order
findings.rationale: ORDER BY on a column no index can deliver in order makes the database sort the whole result first, even when you only want a few rows.
